Name: Father of Greatness
Variants and Titles in Text: Father; God of truth; first established one; King of the lights; first Father
Persian Substrate Name: Ahura Mazda in his transcendent self-subsistent form; Zurvan Akarana (Boundless Time) in Zurvanite tradition as the boundless origin preceding the duality
Persian Literal Reading: Lord of Wisdom (Ahura Mazda) / Boundless Time (Zurvan Akarana)
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The Infinite Divine Love itself — the Lord's own Esse from which all emanations proceed and to which all return; absolute origin of all good and being; established in himself alone without limit or measure; his five limbs (mind, thought, insight, counsel, consideration) are five essential faculties of the Divine Itself; the teaching constantly states he is hidden and immeasurable

Name: Mother of Life
Variants and Titles in Text: Great Spirit; first Holy Spirit; Mother of the living; first Mother
Persian Substrate Name: Spenta Mainyu (Bounteous Spirit)
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: Divine Truth proceeding from Love as the generative matrix of all spiritual life; the womb from which all derivative spiritual states are born; first to emerge from the Father; spent immeasurable time within the Father before being called forth — corresponding to Divine Truth existing in potential within Divine Love before proceeding; mother of the First Man; intercedes for his rescue; she and the Father of Life construct the universe

Name: First Man
Variants and Titles in Text: the Man; blessed Man; living Man; First living Man; Lord as Divine Human
Persian Substrate Name: Ohrmazd / Hormizd
Etymology Note: same root as Ahura Mazda; the good creating spirit in its descending human-facing form
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The Lord as the Celestial Human — the Divine Rational proceeding into combat with the hells; clothed in five garments (five external truths) and descending voluntarily into the deepest states of temptation; prevails through patience and stillness not through force; his five sons remain behind in darkness after his ascent; the first and greatest of all the judges; spent an immeasurable duration in the land of darkness

Name: Living Spirit
Alignment: Realm of Light — Ordering and Rescuing
Variants and Titles in Text: Father of Life; Creator; Architect of the World
Persian Substrate Name: Mihryazd (Mithra as divine being)
Persian Literal Reading: The Divine Covenant / Lord of Covenants
Etymology Note: Mithra is the deity who upholds all compacts and agreements
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The Lord's operative Divine Truth proceeding from Love — the Divine power that rescues, orders, judges, constructs, and sustains the whole spiritual world; rescues the First Man from the abyss; constructs the universe from the bodies of defeated rulers; performs seven complete works of spiritual regeneration; second judge; sends the Summons to the First Man

Name: Third Ambassador
Variants and Titles in Text: Ambassador; King of the Zone; Master of All Advices
Persian Substrate Name: Narisaf / Narisah-yazd (Neryosang in Avestan tradition)
Etymology Note: Naryosanha means literally the envoy or announcer of men; the Manly Envoy
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: Mediating Divine Truth that proceeds into universal manifestation — the Divine principle that purifies wisdom from its admixture with falsity by displaying the Divine image; drawing forth captive good by revealing the Divine likeness; operates through the ships of day and night; sixth judge; second father (called forth by the Father directly); inspects the completed works of creation

Name: Beloved of the Lights
Variants and Titles in Text: the Beloved; Great Honoured Beloved
Persian Substrate Name: Roshan-shah (King of the Lights) — probable Manichaean reconstruction; no direct Avestan attestation
Persian Literal Reading: King of Radiance / King of Lights
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: Divine Good made manifest through Wisdom — the union of love and truth as perceived by all illuminated faculties; second direct emanation from the Father alongside the Great Spirit; humiliates the Darkness; associated with honor and the affectional dimension of the Lord's operation; gives victory to the aeons

Name: Great Builder
Variants and Titles in Text: The Architect; Master Architect
Persian Substrate Name: Bam-yazd — Manichaean period construction; functionally related to Asha Vahishta (Best Righteousness / cosmic order) in Zoroastrian tradition
Etymology Note: Bam means dawn or morning; yazd means deity — the substrate name means the Dawn Deity; rendered as the Dawn
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The Divine Wisdom that organizes understanding into coherent spiritual form — the ordering power that constructs the interior architecture of the regenerating mind; builds the new aeon of joy (new heaven) and a prison for the enemy; fourth judge; works according to plan as a master architect who sees what each piece of unformed good may become

Name: Jesus the Splendour
Variants and Titles in Text: the glorious one; Son of Greatness; Releaser and Redeemer
Persian Substrate Name: Xradeshahr (Splendour of the Realm) in Manichaean Persian; deeper substrate: xvarənah / farr (divine luminous glory) as a cosmic proceeding
Persian Literal Reading: Kingdom of Wisdom / Realm of Right Reason
Etymology Note: Xradeshahr: xrad (wisdom / right reason) + shahr (realm / kingdom)
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The Lord as Divine Wisdom made radiant — Divine Truth in its fullness of glory proceeding to illuminate, liberate, and regenerate; hunts after light and life through wisdom; uproots evil perceptions (the bad fig-garden) and plants the tree of life; fourth day; third father (proceeding from the Ambassador); father of all apostles; eighth judge; enlightens Adam

Name: Pillar of Glory
Variants and Titles in Text: Perfect Man; great porter; Pillar; Column of Glory
Persian Substrate Name: Sraosha (Srosh-ahray in Manichaean Persian) — the Zoroastrian divine being of obedience who upholds cosmic order and carries souls of the righteous
Etymology Note: Sraosha means the act of listening and obeying divine command
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The sustaining Divine Truth connecting all degrees — the fully realized Divine Human form that upholds all spiritual order from the lowest to the highest; the vertical axis through which all influx descends and all purified good ascends; bears all burdens above and below; first of all weight-carriers; seventh judge; its base reaches from the earth to heaven

Name: Virgin of Light
Variants and Titles in Text: Light Virgin; Holy Virgin; Pure Uncorrupted Wisdom
Persian Substrate Name: Kanyag (the Maiden) in Sogdian Manichaean texts; related to Ashi Vanguhi (Good Fortune / celestial maiden) in Zoroastrian tradition
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: Pure uncorrupted wisdom — the affection of truth from good in its pristine celestial innocence; captivates the rulers through her spiritual beauty; draws captive good toward liberation; guides the new man; robes the soul at the moment of life; third emanation of the Ambassador; ninth judge; called 'the hour of life — she is the first but she is also the last'

Name: Light Mind
Variants and Titles in Text: The Mind; Awakener; Gatherer of the Scattered
Persian Substrate Name: Wahman / Vohu Manah (Good Mind / Good Thought) — first and most important of the Amesha Spentas
Etymology Note: Vohu Manah: vohu (good) + manah (mind / thought)
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The Lord's Divine Wisdom entering and operating within the human understanding — the interior illumination that regenerates the person; descends into the individual body; binds the old man with five counsels; loosens the soul's faculties from falsity; constructs the new man with five living members (love, faith, perfection, patience, wisdom); fourth father; eleventh judge

Name: Great Judge (Judge of Truth)
Variants and Titles in Text: The Judge; Judge of the Atmosphere
Persian Substrate Name: Rashnu — the Zoroastrian divine weigher of souls at the Chinvat Bridge; holds the scales of absolute judgment; third member of the bridge-tribunal alongside Mithra (Living Spirit) and Sraosha (Pillar of Glory)
Etymology Note: Rashnu means justice or rightness in the sense of the cosmic scales
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: Divine Truth as it performs separation and judgment in the intermediate state; dwells in the atmosphere and judges all mankind; makes the final separation between the righteous and the sinners; three paths are distinguished before him: to death, to life, to the mingling; tenth judge; second power summoned by Jesus the Splendour

Name: The Youth (Jesus the Youth)
Variants and Titles in Text: Jesus the Youth; Image of the Living Word
Persian Substrate Name: Unknown — Meshyag is a tentative Manichaean scholarly reconstruction without strong Avestan precedent
Etymology Note: Meshyag may relate to the primordial human; literal meaning unclear
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The image of the living Word — the active reception of influx in the natural mind; the first responsive form placed in the elements; formed by Jesus the Splendour and set there as the image of utterance and obedience; third power summoned by Jesus the Splendour

Name: Apostle of Light
Variants and Titles in Text: Apostle; Messenger; Transmitter
Persian Substrate Name: Frēstag (messenger / envoy in Manichaean Persian)
Etymology Note: Frestag means one who is sent forth on a mission
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The function of communicating sacred truth to the human mind — the cosmic principle of transmission that sends divine knowledge into the world; appears in time to transmit knowledge; first power of the Light Mind (fourth father); ninth throne; precedes all earthly apostles as their cosmic archetype

Name: The Counterpart (Companion to the Apostle)
Variants and Titles in Text: The Twin; Companion; Syzygos
Persian Substrate Name: Narig (the precious one) in Manichaean texts; corresponds to the Fravashi (heavenly double / guardian spirit) in Zoroastrian tradition
Persian Literal Reading: The Precious One / The Dear One
Etymology Note: Narig means precious or beloved
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The interior celestial perception that accompanies the external communication of truth — the divine twin of the apostle; provides help from all afflictions and dangers; becomes companion sticking close everywhere; corresponds to the heavenly double that every soul possesses in the celestial world; second power of the Light Mind

Name: Light Form
Alignment: Realm of Light — Terminal and Initial
Variants and Titles in Text: Form of Light; Redeemer of the Soul; the Daena
Persian Substrate Name: Daena (the soul's own divine image in Zoroastrian tradition) — appears at the Chinvat Bridge as either beautiful or hideous depending on the soul's deeds; in the Ardā Wirāz Nāmag, appears as a radiant maiden to the righteous
Etymology Note: Daena is the soul's own accumulated nature made visible to itself
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The spiritual state that appears at the threshold of death to gather the soul into peace; calms the dying person with kiss and quiet; corresponds to what the person has become interiorly; fifth father; attended by three angels bearing prize, garment, and crown; she is 'the first but she is also the last' — both first origin and final return

Name: Three Angels of the Light Form
Variants and Titles in Text: Prize-bearer; Garment-bearer; Crown-bearer (possessing the diadem, wreath, and crown of light)
Persian Substrate Name: Unknown by name; correspond to the three categories of heavenly reward at the Chinvat Bridge in Zoroastrian tradition
Etymology Note: functional descriptions only (prize-bearer, garment-bearer, crown-bearer)
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: Three celestial figures attending the Light Form at the moment of death: the first holds the victory prize; the second bears the light garment; the third possesses the diadem, wreath, and crown of light. They correspond to three degrees of heavenly reward — the outward recognition of celestial good, spiritual truth, and natural works accomplished in life

Name: Summons (The Call)
Variants and Titles in Text: The Call; The First Voice
Persian Substrate Name: Xvash khvan (sweet caller / sweet voice) in Manichaean Persian; the initiating divine voice
Etymology Note: Xvash khvan: xvash (sweet / pleasant) + khvan (caller / voice)
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The Lord's active calling forth of divine truth — the active influx of truth from the Divine into the human will; sent from the Living Spirit to the captive First Man; penetrates the deepest states of captivity and initiates liberation; always active and descending; together with Obedience constitutes twenty-five characteristics in twenty-five limbs; opened the portals of mercy; one of the twelve hours of the Pillar

Name: Obedience (The Answer)
Variants and Titles in Text: The Answer; The Hearing
Persian Substrate Name: Ashtag (implied in Manichaean Persian texts)
Etymology Note: tentative; Sraosha already covers this function in Zoroastrian tradition
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The will's willing reception of divine truth — the responsive ascent of good toward the Lord's calling; ascends from the First Man back to the Living Spirit; completes the circuit of influx; always receptive and ascending; like a letter written from the battlefield disclosing all the states of temptation to the Divine; together with the Summons opened the portals of mercy for the First Man

Name: Last Statue
Variants and Titles in Text: The Statue; The Grand Man
Persian Substrate Name: Tan-i-Pasen (Final Body) in Manichaean Persian — attested in Middle Persian texts; no direct pre-Manichaean Persian equivalent identified
Persian Literal Reading: The Final Body / The Completed Form
Etymology Note: Tan-i-Pasen: tan (body) + pasen (final / last)
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The fully realized Divine Human form — the completed Grand Man constituted of all gathered and purified goods and truths; sculpts itself at the final consummation from the remnant of all things; the collective form of all redeemed good in its final perfection; when complete it ascends to the aeon of light through the Living Spirit; the ultimate goal of the entire arc of regeneration

Name: Five Sons of the First Man (Five Light Elements)
Variants and Titles in Text: Five Garments; Five Shining Gods; Living Elements; Five Sons
Persian Substrate Name: Amesha Spentas (the five Holy Immortals when the Father is set apart from the count); in Manichaean Middle Persian: the five elements as five divine beings with the names of the five Amesha Spentas
Etymology Note: individually the names are qualities: Good Mind / Best Truth / Desired Dominion / Holy Devotion / Wholeness (Amesha Spentas: amesha = immortal; spenta = holy)
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The five faculties of celestial perception serving as the armor of the First Man in temptation-combat: Consideration (outermost — holy church), Counsel (Pillar of Glory), Insight (First Man's ship of night), Thought (Ambassador's ship of day), Mind (the Father in aeons of light). Devoured by darkness during the first combat; bind darkness from within; remain captive until gathered into the Last Statue. Together with Summons and Obedience they constitute the twelve hours of the third day

Name: Five Sons of the Living Spirit
Variants and Titles in Text: Five Structural Gods; Supporters of the World; Five Sons
Persian Substrate Name: Panj Roshan (the Five Luminous Ones) — attested in Manichaean Middle Persian texts as the group name for the five sons of the Living Spirit
Persian Literal Reading: The Five Luminous Ones / The Five Bright Ones
Etymology Note: Panj Roshan: panj (five) + roshan (luminous / bright)
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The five structural powers that sustain the spiritual world and restrain the hells — distinct from the First Man's five sons which are faculties of perception; these are the structural skeleton of the cosmos: the disc on the Porter's shoulder, the arches before him, the mould of the gehennas, the seven pillars in the great sea, the four walls surrounding the vessels; together with the First Man's five sons they constitute the twelve aeons of light (5+5+2)

Name: Keeper of Splendour
Variants and Titles in Text: Omophorus; Mind of the World Above
Persian Substrate Name: Xroshtagarbed (Guardian of the realm-radiance) — tentative Manichaean scholarly reconstruction; Splenditenens in Latin Manichaean sources
Persian Literal Reading: Guardian of the Radiance / Holder of Splendour
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The Divine protection over the highest rational degree of the mind — Mind of the world above; stationed in the camp above the prison of the bound ones; brings to nothing all the gloom of death; governs the three upper heavens; corresponds to the face and upper perceptions in the body; master of the first watch-station

Name: King of Honour
Variants and Titles in Text: The Great King of Honour; Thought of the Seventh Firmament
Persian Substrate Name: Visbed (Ruler of territories / lands) — tentative Manichaean scholarly reconstruction
Persian Literal Reading: Ruler of the Settled Lands / Lord of the Territories
Etymology Note: Visbed: vis (settlement / clan) + bed (lord / ruler)
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The Divine governance within the interior rational degree — Thought of the seventh firmament; governs the seven heavens; the will as heart governing all rational degrees; seated on the great throne of honor at the center of the universe; the King of Honour before whom the wheel of Providence stands; corresponds to the heart in the body

Name: Adamant of Light
Variants and Titles in Text: Adamant; Splenditenens; Insight of the Higher World
Persian Substrate Name: Zandbed (Life-champion / unyielding guardian) — tentative Manichaean scholarly reconstruction
Etymology Note: Zandbed: zand (living / vital) + bed (lord / ruler)
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The unyielding power of Divine Truth against the assaults of the proprium — Insight of the higher world; stationed in the middle region; smites the sea giant; subdues Matter; governs from the firmament down to the earth; master of the third watch-station; holds the sphere steady; corresponds to the genitals (generative truth) in the body

Name: King of Glory
Variants and Titles in Text: Great Counsel; Master of the Three Wheels
Persian Substrate Name: Manbed (Mind-ruler) — tentative Manichaean scholarly reconstruction
Etymology Note: Manbed: man (mind / thought) + bed (lord / ruler)
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The Divine Truth that directs the ascent of influx through the three wheels of wind, water, and fire — Counsel and Patience; master of the fourth watch-station; turns the three wheels; sends the life above; governs the three earths above the Porter; corresponds to the stomach and the fire within in the body

Name: Porter (Atlas)
Variants and Titles in Text: Atlas; The Consideration and Wisdom of the Earth Below
Persian Substrate Name: Fravahr (guardian spirit archetype) — tentative; the Porter's foundational sustaining function relates broadly to the Fravashi concept of the sustaining heavenly double in Zoroastrian tradition
Persian Literal Reading: Protective Spirit / Heavenly Double / Guardian Soul
Etymology Note: Fravahr is every person's pre-existing heavenly archetype that precedes and outlasts them
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The sustaining foundation of truth in the lowest natural degree — Consideration and Wisdom of the Earth; bears the foundation below all the earths; subdues the uprising of the abyss with his footsoles; master of the fifth watch-station; the four cosmic fastenings are under his feet; corresponds to the feet and soles in the body; the outermost reception holding everything above it

Name: King of Darkness
Variants and Titles in Text: Ruler of Smoke; Chief of Demons; Head of All Wickedness; King of the realms of Darkness
Persian Substrate Name: Ahriman (Angra Mainyu)
Etymology Note: Angra Mainyu: angra (destructive / harmful) + mainyu (spirit / mind)
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The ruling principle of self-love — the sovereign evil that governs all states of falsity from evil; the love of dominion from self that is the head of all hells; five shapes on his body correspond to five genera of evil; body harder than all iron and copper; can hide himself through persuasive falsity (magic arts); knows only what is immediately before him (no foresight); organized all darkness for the assault against the realm of light; first judge of evil

Name: King of the Worlds of Fire (Lion-faced)
Variants and Titles in Text: The Lion-Faced King of Fire; foremost of all the beasts
Persian Substrate Name: Ēšm / Aēšma (demon of Wrath) — lion = dominating predatory power; Probable
Etymology Note: Aeshma means wrath or assault in Avestan
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: Consuming self-love and the hatred of good — the demonic principle of fire ruling through lust and domination; copper body; sour taste; manifests in the world as fire-worshipping sects and leaders driven by the love of power over others

Name: King of the Worlds of Wind (Eagle-faced)
Variants and Titles in Text: The Eagle-Faced King of Wind
Persian Substrate Name: Aēšma-daēva (demon of wrath and assault); eagle = predatory rationality seizing from above — Tentative
Etymology Note: Aeshma-daeva: daeva adds demon to the wrath concept
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: Predatory rationality and false persuasions — the demonic principle of wind ruling through sharp and cutting argument; iron body; sharp taste; manifests as idolatry — spirits of error dwelling in temples, statues, and images

Name: King of the World of Water (Fish-faced)
Variants and Titles in Text: The Fish-Faced King of Water
Persian Substrate Name: Apaosha (demon opposing water and natural life); fish = submersion in falsity without ascent — Tentative
Persian Literal Reading: That Which Withholds Rain / Drought Demon
Etymology Note: Apaosha means the withholding of water or nourishment
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The seductive delight of falsified truth — the demonic principle of water ruling through deceptive sweetness; silver body; sweet taste; the most dangerous darkness because it presents falsity as desirable; manifests as sects that baptize with water, setting hope in the external rite

Name: King of the World of Darkness (Dragon)
Variants and Titles in Text: The Dragon King; King of Lead
Persian Substrate Name: Azi Dahāka (the dragon-demon of Iranian mythology); the dragon = comprehensive falsification of all truth — Probable
Persian Literal Reading: The Biting Serpent / The Wounding Dragon
Etymology Note: Azi Dahaka: azi (serpent) + dahaka (biting / wounding)
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The densest, basest falsity — the demonic principle of pure darkness; body of lead and tin; bitter taste; manifests as soothsayers, oracles, possessed ones, and diviners; corresponds to the lowest natural mind wholly given over to evil; the ultimate compaction of falsehood

Name: Matter (The Sculptress / Thought of Death)
Variants and Titles in Text: The Sculptress; Thought of Death; Mother of All Evil Fruits
Persian Substrate Name: Āz (demon of concupiscence / greed in Zurvanite tradition) and / or Jeh (the demonic feminine); Āz is the active formative evil that animates all darkness
Persian Literal Reading: Greed / Concupiscence (Az) and The Demonic Feminine (Jeh)
Etymology Note: Az means simply greed or lust; Jeh is the demoness of licentiousness
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The proprium — the self-derived will that gives form to all evil and falsity; fashions the worlds of darkness; gives strength to the King of Darkness for war; the mother of all evil affections; sculpts the body of evil from the nature of the land of darkness; 'the thought of death' = the proprium conceived not as inert substance but as an active intention toward spiritual death; the womb from which all particular evils are born

Name: Law of Sin (Dark Spirit)
Variants and Titles in Text: Dark Spirit; Law of Death; The Night
Persian Substrate Name: Druj / Drug (the Lie / Falsity as a cosmic power in Avestan tradition) — the opposite of Asha (Truth / Righteousness)
Etymology Note: Druj or Drug is a single word meaning the Lie as an active cosmic force opposing Asha (Truth)
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The ruling principle of falsity in the natural mind — the fourth night; speaks in the twelve zodiacal signs; the twelve signs are called 'the nakednesses' and 'Matter's thrones'; corresponds to the animating spirit of all organized falsity from evil; the fourth dark operation that ensnares spiritual life through constant deception

Name: Sea Giant
Variants and Titles in Text: The Residue; The Monster of the Depths
Persian Substrate Name: Gōchihr (Manichaean / Zurvanite cosmic dragon or comet-body) — formed from the residue of the cosmic purification process; attested in Manichaean texts
Etymology Note: Gochihr relates to the primordial bull whose death seeds the world
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The monstrous composite selfhood formed from the residue of all sensory knowledge and cosmic cycles; sculpted from the waste of the wheel of the sphere by its own lust; bears the seals of all stars and zodiacal signs on its body; acts as hostel for cosmic waste and residue; is nailed to the wheel by the Adamant of Light between the mountains; drags back the sphere when it would rise; corresponds to the monstrous proprium formed within the mass of natural knowledge

Name: Saklas (and his consort)
Variants and Titles in Text: The Fool; The Sculptor of Adam
Persian Substrate Name: Substrate Persian name unknown — the Saklas designation is Sethian / Gnostic overlay (Aramaic: fool / the demiurge); the substrate figure was probably a Persian demonological name for the chief constructive agent of Ahriman; possibly a functional title of Āz in its active-fashioning mode
Etymology Note: this is Aramaic not Persian; the Persian substrate name is lost
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The malformed creator principle — self-derived intelligence that imitates divine action without receiving it; fashions Adam and Eve as counterfeit copies of the Ambassador's image using appropriated light from his companions; chief of the abortions; 'they copied it against the image of the exalted one — but not in truth; just as an image seen in water'; corresponds to the constructive power of the proprium when it claims what flows through it

Name: Adam (First Man of Flesh)
Variants and Titles in Text: The First Man of Flesh; Adam the First
Persian Substrate Name: Gayomard / Kayomars (primordial human in Iranian tradition); on his death his seed produces the first human couple; 'the seal of the entire universe is stamped upon Adam'
Etymology Note: Gayomard: gay (life / living) + mard (mortal / man)
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The Most Ancient Church — the natural human containing the divine likeness; formed by the abortions after the Ambassador's image; three great things distinguish him: the image of the exalted one, organization through the five sons, and the inscription of all celestial correspondences; archetype of the natural mind in which the cosmos is recapitulated in miniature; the battlefield of the Light Mind against the old man

Name: Eve (Adam's Consort)
Variants and Titles in Text: The First Woman; Adam's Consort
Persian Substrate Name: Mashyanay (first woman of Iranian tradition; with Mashyag the first human couple born from Gayomard's seed in the earth)
Persian Literal Reading: The Mortal One / The Human Female
Etymology Note: Mashyanay is the feminine form of Mashya meaning the mortal one
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: The receptive affection of the natural mind — the womb of human generation; enlightened by Jesus the Splendour; the will as it first receives the impression of the divine likeness; mother of all subsequent generations; the feminine receptive principle in the human soul

Name: Five Stars (Planetary Rulers)
Variants and Titles in Text: Zeus-star (Jupiter); Aphrodite-star (Venus); Ares-star (Mars); Hermes-star (Mercury); Cronos-star (Saturn) — Greek Layer 2 names for Persian planetary beings
Persian Substrate Name: Ohrmazd-star (Jupiter = Ohrmazd); Anahit-star (Venus = Anahita); Wahram-star (Mars = Bahram); Tir-star (Mercury = Tir); Keywān-star (Saturn = Keywān) — attested in Persian astrology
Persian Literal Reading: Star of Lord Wisdom (Jupiter) / Star of the Immaculate One (Venus) / Star of Victory (Mars) / Star of the Swift Arrow (Mercury) / Star of the Slow-Mover (Saturn)
Correspondential Spiritual Meaning: Five principal evil affections seized from the five dark worlds and bound upon the revolving sphere: Jupiter from the world of Smoke (mind / perverted intellect), Venus from Fire (self-love), Mars from Wind (predatory rationality), Mercury from Water (falsified truth), Saturn from Darkness (basest falsity). They are all enemies and rivals to each other. The sun and moon — strangers among them belonging to the greatness — subjugate them at every moment
